levels.name: Pip, 23, Junior Intern
levels.story: The 8 levels of faking expertise in high-stakes meetings. Level 1. Level 1: 0 percent expertise in Q1 strategy, and my stomach is doing backflips. I am Pip, a 23-year-old strawberry with bruised skin, sitting at the end of the mahogany boardroom table clutching a $4 spiral notepad. You brought zero data to this massive $4 million pitch meeting, Pip. My heart hammers against my ribs, sweat drips down my leafy green stem, and my hands shake so hard I drop my cheap plastic pen. Then I remember the finance podcast I listened to while scrubbing toilets this morning, take a deep breath, and lean into the microphone. You have to leverage synergistic cross-platform liquidity before scaling Q3 deliverables. The entire executive board stops breathing. You'll see that in Level 2.

levels.name: Leo, 28, Assistant Manager
levels.story: The 8 levels of faking expertise in high-stakes meetings. Level 2. Level 2: 12 percent expertise is enough to get you scheduled for an agonizing morning review. I am Leo, a bright orange citrus man whose rind is turning pale from sheer panic in Room 402. Look at the orange, he doesn't even know what a pivot table is. My rent just jumped to $2,100 in downtown Produce City, and my boss expects me to lead a marketing breakdown on blockchain logistics. I copied three slides from Wikipedia five minutes ago while waiting for my oat milk latte. Halfway through my slide about decentralized algorithms, my screen flickers and opens a YouTube tutorial titled Basic Excel for Dummies. Then the office door swings wide open. You'll see that in Level 3.

levels.name: Max, 34, Senior Analyst
levels.story: The 8 levels of faking expertise in high-stakes meetings. Level 3. Level 3: 35 percent expertise and a tailored suit that cost me two weeks of grocery money. I am Max, an Avocado man whose smooth green skin is glistening under the harsh LED panels of the corporate atrium. Look at him pretending to lead when his suit is clearly from three seasons ago. Everyone thinks I am heading the quarterly tax restructuring, but my entire strategy relies on using big words like macro-economic headwinds. My mortgage is $2,800 a month, and my bank account is sitting at a terrifying $42. We must recalibrate our fiscal parameters to align with global market velocity. Then my phone buzzes with a notification that exposes my true balance. You'll see that in Level 4.

levels.name: Chloe, 26, Data Analyst
levels.story: The 8 levels of faking expertise in high-stakes meetings. Level 4. Level 4: 50 percent expertise and I am currently faking an entire supply chain audit. I am Chloe, a Lemon woman whose yellow rind is pinched into a sour grimace as I stare at the glowing spreadsheet. You call this rigorous statistical modeling, Chloe? It looks like third-grade guesswork. My student loans are $34,000, and my studio apartment rent just went up to $2,300. The director of operations towers over my desk, demanding proof for projections I completely guessed yesterday. I used a random number generator for the logistics growth curve, and now the CEO wants a full presentation in ten minutes. Then the printer behind me suddenly starts spitting out an unauthorized audit report. You'll see that in Level 5.
